Glossary

abhidhamma the higher teachings of Buddhism, teachings on ultimate realities. non aversion. adosa unwholesome, unskilful. akusala non attachment, generosity. alobha wisdom or understanding. amoha non-returner, person who has reached the third stage of enlightenment, he has anāgāmī no aversion (dosa). not self. anattā impermanence. anicca absorption. appanā noble person who has attained the fourth and last stage of enlightenment. arahat object which is known by consciousness. ārammaṇa noble person who has attained enlightenment. ariyan arūpa-bhūmi plane of arūpa jhānacitta. arūpa-brahma plane plane of existence attained as a result of arūpa-jhāna. There are no sense impressions, no rūpa experienced in this realm. arūpa-jhāna immaterial absorption. influxes or intoxicants, group of defilements . āsavas not beautiful, not accompanied by beautiful roots. asobhana foul. asubha demon, being of one of the unhappy planes of existence. asura Atthasālinī The Expositor, a commentary to the first book of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka. ignorance. avijjā ayoniso manasikāra unwise attention to an object. mental development, comprising the development of calm and the development bhāvanā of insight. life-continuum. bhavanga

monk. bhikkhu bhikkhunī nun. plane of existence or plane of citta. bhūmi brahma-vihāras the four divine abidings, meditation subjects which are: loving kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, equanimity. a fully enlightened person who has discovered the truth all by himself, without Buddha the aid of a teacher and can proclaim Dhamma to the world. Buddhaghosa commentator on the Tipiṭaka, author of the Visuddhimagga in 5 A.D. eye. cakkhu volition or intention. cetanā mental factor arising with consciousness. cetasika consciousness, the reality which knows or cognizes an object. citta cuti-citta dying-consciousness. generosity, giving. dāna reality, truth, the teachings. dhamma Dhammasangaṇi the first book of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka. Dhātukathā Discussion on the Elements, the third book of the Abhidhamma. wrong view, distorted view of realities. diṭṭhi domanassa unpleasant feeling. aversion or ill will. dosa dosa-mūla-citta citta (consciousness) rooted in aversion. suffering, unsatisfactoriness of conditioned realities. dukkha dukkha vedanā painful feeling or unpleasant feeling. doorway through which an object is experienced, the five sense-doors or the dvāra mind door. concentration, one-pointedness, a cetasika which has the function to focus on ekaggatā one object. bonds, a group of defilements. ganthas

Glossary 131

ghāna-dhātu nose element. change of lineage, the last citta of the sense-sphere before jhāna, absorption, is gotrabhū attained, or enlightenment is attained. hadaya-vatthu heart-base, rūpa which is the plane of origin of the cittas other than the sensecognitions. hasituppāda-citta smile producing consciousness of an arahat. root, which conditions citta to be “beautiful” or unwholesome. hetu faculty. Some are rūpas such as the sense organs, some are nāmas such as feeling. indriya Five ’spiritual faculties’ are wholesome faculties which should be cultivated, namely: confidence, energy, awareness, concentration and wisdom. envy. issā birth, nature, class (of cittas). jāti javana-citta cittas which ’run through the object’, kusala citta or akusala citta in the case of non-arahats. absorption which can be attained through the development of calm. jhāna jhāna-factors cetasikas which have to be cultivated for the attainment of jhāna: vitakka, vicāra, pīti, sukha, samādhi. sensual enjoyment or the five sense objects. kāma kāma-bhūmi sensuous plane of existence. kāmacchandha sensuous desire. kāma-sobhana cittas beautiful cittas of the sense sphere. kāmāvacara cittas cittas of the sense sphere. intention or volition; deed motivated by volition. kamma kammapatha course of action performed through body, speech or mind which can be wholesome or unwholesome. compassion. karuṇā disk, used as an object for the development of calm. kasiṇa body. It can also stand for the “mental body”, the cetasikas. kāya

aggregates of conditioned realities classified as five groups: physical phenomena, khandhas feelings, perception or remembrance, activities or formations (cetasikas other than feeling or perception), consciousness. defilements. kilesa kiriya citta inoperative citta, neither cause nor result. regret or worry. kukkucca kusala citta wholesome consciousness. kusala kamma a good deed. wholesome, skillful. kusala attachment, greed. lobha lobha-mūla-citta consciousness rooted in attachment. macchariya stinginess. path (eightfold Path). magga magga-citta path consciousness, supramundane citta which experiences nibbāna and eradicates defilements. mahā-kusala citta wholesome citta of the sense sphere. mahā-vipākacitta citta of the sense sphere which is result, accompanied by “beautiful” roots. manāyatana mind-base, including all cittas. mind, citta, consciousness. mano “the evil one”—all that leads to dukkha māra loving kindness. mettā torpor or languor. middha ignorance. moha-mūla-citta citta rooted in ignorance. moha sympathetic joy. muditā mental phenomena, including those which are conditioned and also the uncon- nāma ditioned nāma which is nibbāna. the unconditioned reality, the reality which does not arise and fall away.The nibbāna destruction of lust, hatred and delusion. The deathless. The end of suffering.

Glossary 133

mental image one can acquire of a meditation subject in tranquil meditation. nimitta nirodha-samāpatti attainment of cessation of consciousness. hindrances, a group of defilements. nīvaraṇa wisdom, insight. ~nāṇa Pacceka Buddha Silent Buddha, an enlightened one who has found the truth by himself but does not proclaim Dhamma to the world. Conditional Relations, the seventh book of the Abhidhamma. Paṭṭhāna paṭisandhi citta rebirth consciousness. the language of the Buddhist teachings. Pāli wisdom or understanding. pa~n~nā concepts, conventional terms. pa~n~natti paramattha dhamma truth in the absolute sense: mental and physical phenomena, each with their own characteristic. joy, rapture, enthusiasm. pīti puthujjana “worldling”, a person who has not attained enlightenment. the Buddha’s son. Rāhula physical phenomena, realities which do not experience anything. rūpa rūpa-brahma plane rūpa-bhūmi, fine material realm of existence attained as a result of rūpajhāna. rūpa-jhāna fine material absorption, developed with a meditation subject which is still dependant on materiality. rūpa-khandha aggregate or group of all physical phenomena (rūpas). rūpāvacara cittas rūpa-jhānacittas, consciousness of the fine-material sphere. confidence. saddhā sakadāgāmī once-returner, a noble person who has attained the second stage of enlightenment. concentration or one-pointedness, ekaggatā cetasika. samādhi

the development of calm. samatha right. sammā community of monks and nuns. As one of the triple Gems it means the com- Sangha munity of those people who have attained enlightenment. . memory, remembrance or “perception”. sa~n~nā mindfulness or awareness: non-forgetfulness of what is wholesome, or non- sati forgetfulness of realities which appear. satipaṭṭhāna sutta Middle Length Sayings 1, number 10, also Dīgha Nikāya, Dialogues, no. 22. satipaṭṭhāna applications of mindfulness. It can mean the cetasika sati which is aware of realities or the objects of mindfulness which are classified as four applications of mindfulness: Body, Feeling Citta, Dhamma. Or it can mean the development of direct understanding of realities through awareness. morality in action or speech, virtue. sīla somanassa happy feeling. sotāpanna person who has attained the first stage of enlightenment, and who has eradicated wrong view of realities. happy, pleasant. sukha sukha-vedanā pleasant feeling.

part of the scriptures containing dialogues at different places on different occa- sutta sions. a sutta text. suttanta Tathāgata literally “thus gone”, epithet of the Buddha. tatramajjhattatā equanimity or even-mindedness. Theravāda Buddhism ‘Doctrine of the Elders’, the oldest tradition of Buddhism. sloth. thīna the teachings of the Buddha contained in the Vinaya, the Suttanta and the Tipiṭaka Abhidhamma. restlessness. uddhacca Verses of Uplift from the Minor Anthologies. clinging. upādāna upādāna-kkhandhas khandhas of clinging. indifferent feeling. It can stand for even-mindedness or equanimity and then it upekkhā is not feeling. vāyo-dhātu element of wind or motion. feeling. vedanā vedanā-kkhandha group of all feelings. “Book of Analysis”, second book of the Abhidhamma. Vibha_nga

Book of Discipline for the monks. vinaya consciousness, citta. vi~n~nāṇa vi~n~nāṇa-dhātu element of consciousness, comprising all cittas. vi~n~nāṇa-kkhandha group of all cittas (consciousness). vipākacitta citta which is the result of a wholesome deed (kusala kamma) or an unwholesome deed (akusala kamma). It can arise as rebirth- consciousness, or during life as the experience of pleasant or unpleasant objects through the senses, such as seeing, hearing, etc. vipassanā wisdom which sees realities as they are. energy. viriya Visuddhimagga an Encyclopedia of the Buddha’s teachings, written by Buddhaghosa in the fifth century A.D. the Book of Pairs, the sixth book of the Abhidhamma. Yamaka yoniso manasikāra wise attention to the object.
